events.excerpt: One year to go for T+1 settlement: the regulatory framework is complete, now let’s make it happen 16 October 2026 Guidelines and Technical standards Post Trading Press Releases The European Union (EU) will switch to T+1 settlement on 11 October 2027. Ahead of the transition, the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA), the EU’s financial markets regulator and supervisor, calls on market participants to finalise technical preparations, assess readiness across their entire ecosystems and begin testing as soon as possible throughout the trading and settlement chain. With the publication of the RTS and ESMA Guidelines on standardised procedures and messaging protocols , the regulatory framework is now ready. The first deadline is for investment firms and their clients to comply with the new requirements on allocations and confirmations from 7 December 2026. Verena Ross, ESMA’s chair, said: “The transition to T+1 is one of the most impactful recent market structure initiatives. It will fundamentally improve the efficiency and international competitiveness of the EU markets. events.excerpt: ESMA streamlines several Q&As as part of simplification efforts 22 October 2026 Market Abuse MiFID - Secondary Markets Short Selling Simplification and Burden Reduction The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA), the EU regulator and supervisor, has updated its Questions and Answers (Q&As) on market structure under MiFID II , the Market Abuse Regulation (MAR) and the Short Selling Regulation (SSR) , removing outdated, duplicative and no longer relevant guidance as part of its Simplification and Burden Reduction (SBR) initiative . The exercise focused on identifying Q&As that are no longer relevant due to legislative amendments that are reflected in established market practices, or that are covered by other ESMA guidance. As a result, several Q&As have been withdrawn or amended, including instances where the same issues are addressed in other ESMA publications such as supervisory briefings and opinions. The goal of the initiative is to reduce unnecessary complexity, remove obsolete guidance and ensure that ESMA's Q&As remain relevant, proportionate and consistent with the current legislative framework. Stakeholders are encouraged to refer to the updated set of Q&As together with any other ESMA guidance for the most comprehensive interpretation of the applicable rules. Fu
